title: Claimed Proof & Lean Formalization of Sogge’s 1991 Local Smoothing Conjecture
whyItMatters: Claims a complete resolution of Sogge’s 1991 Local Smoothing Conjecture in all dimensions n ≥ 2—the apex conjecture implying Bochner–Riesz, Fourier Restriction, and Kakeya.
summary: Released in the openai/math repository on October 25, 2026 alongside OpenAI’s ETH refutation, a 59-page AI-generated preprint and accompanying Lean 4 formalization claim a full proof of Christopher Sogge’s 1991 Local Smoothing Conjecture for the Euclidean wave equation in every spatial dimension n ≥ 2 via a novel auxiliary PDE construction. Because Local Smoothing sits at the top of harmonic analysis’s classical implication hierarchy—implying the Bochner–Riesz, Fourier Restriction, and Kakeya conjectures—harmonic analyst Alex Iosevich described it as a potential 'historic development' pending full expert refereeing.
technicalHighlights: Claims optimal L^p local smoothing estimates for the Euclidean wave equation across all spatial dimensions n ≥ 2 (open since Sogge 1991).
Introduces an AI-devised auxiliary PDE argument designed to bypass decades of decoupling and Kakeya bottlenecks.
Published openly in openai/math with both a 59-page LaTeX paper and accompanying Lean 4 formalization files for community audit.
caveats: Remains an unrefereed preprint under active specialist review. As with other late-2026 self-published Lean dumps from openai/math, independent harmonic analysts must confirm that the Lean statements match the exact classical L^p space-time estimates without hidden hypotheses or scope gaps.

scoreRationale.foundational: If confirmed, resolves the crowning open conjecture of Euclidean harmonic analysis since 1991, simultaneously implying Bochner–Riesz, Restriction, and Kakeya.
scoreRationale.ripple: Would reshape modern Fourier analysis, dispersive PDEs, and geometric measure theory overnight.
scoreRationale.verification: Scored conservatively because despite accompanying Lean files, independent specialist audit and journal refereeing have not yet certified the claim.
scoreRationale.velocity: Autonomous AI discovery of a claimed all-dimension proof via a new auxiliary PDE technique.
